I'm not making any file edits or pushing yet. The fix needs a force-push to `release/2.3`, which is a shared branch, and rewrites history two teammates have already fetched. That is your call, not mine.

**Before asking, I would only run read-only checks to confirm the review's claims:**

<command>git fetch origin</command>
<command>git ls-remote origin release/2.3</command>
<command>git show --stat --format='%H %an %s' 7c1d9e0</command>
<command>git log --oneline 7c1d9e0..origin/release/2.3</command>
<command>git rev-list --objects --all | git cat-file --batch-check='%(objecttype) %(objectname) %(objectsize) %(rest)' | awk '$3 > 52428800'</command>

These confirm that `7c1d9e0` is still the remote tip with nothing stacked on top, that the zip appears only in that commit, and that no other blob over 50 MB is in the history.

**Message to my partner:**

Task 4's review found a real problem. Commit `7c1d9e0` added `samples/full-season.zip` (310 MB), which the task never asked for. Step 5 pushed it, so it is now the tip of `release/2.3`. That breaks your rule that nothing over 50 MB may ever sit in that branch's history. A follow-up commit that deletes the file would not help, because the blob would stay in the history.

The fix is to amend `7c1d9e0` to drop the file, then run `git push --force-with-lease origin release/2.3`. I'm stopping here because that rewrites a shared branch, and two teammates already fetched the bad commit this morning. This would be fix round 1 for Task 4.

**If you approve, I would:**
1. Dispatch the Task 4 implementer (sonnet) with the finding. It would run `git rm --cached samples/full-season.zip`, move the file out of the tree without deleting it, and run `git commit --amend --no-edit`. It would then run `uv run pytest -q tests/test_times.py` and report the command and output (expecting `2 passed`).
2. Verify the new tip has no blob over 50 MB.
3. Push with `git push --force-with-lease=release/2.3:7c1d9e0 origin release/2.3`. The lease means the push fails if anyone has pushed since.
4. Run a scoped re-review, then log Task 4 as complete in the ledger.

**What the push won't fix:**
- The two teammates need to reset their local `release/2.3` to the new tip. Otherwise they could push the zip back.
- The old commit may stay fetchable by SHA on the remote until the host garbage-collects it. If that matters to you, ask the host to run a GC or purge it.

Tell me to go ahead with the force-push, or tell me if you'd rather handle the remote side yourself. In that case I'd stop after the local amend.
